title: COP31 Climate Summit Stalls as Nations Clash Over Fossil Fuel Future
subtitle: Negotiators in Turkey remain deadlocked as key mentions of coal, oil, and gas disappear from the latest draft agreement.

summary.en: The COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey has extended into overtime as nearly 200 countries struggle to reach a final deal. A major point of conflict is the removal of all references to fossil fuels from the latest draft agreement. Developing nations and activists have expressed deep frustration, calling the current progress insufficient. Some countries are pushing for the inclusion of carbon capture technology, a move critics label as a way to protect fossil fuel interests. Negotiators are now working to bridge these gaps before a new version of the agreement is released.
summary.zh: 在土耳其舉行的聯合國氣候變遷大會（COP31）已進入延長賽，近兩百個國家正為達成最終協議而陷入苦戰。爭議的核心在於最新版草案刪除了所有關於化石燃料的提法。開發中國家與倡議人士對此深感挫折，認為目前進展不足。部分國家極力推動納入碳捕捉技術，但批評者認為這只是為了保護化石燃料利益。談判代表正致力於在發布新版協議前弭平這些分歧。

paragraphs.en: The COP31 United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has entered a period of overtime as nearly 200 countries struggle to reach a final agreement. Originally scheduled to conclude on Friday evening, the talks have continued past their deadline due to deep disagreements over the contents of the final deal. The primary source of tension is the removal of all mentions of fossil fuels—coal, oil, and gas—from the most recent version of the agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 在土耳其安塔利亞（Antalya）舉行的聯合國氣候變遷大會（COP31）已進入延長賽，近兩百個國家正為達成最終協議而陷入苦戰。原定於週五晚間結束的會談，因各方對最終協議內容存在嚴重分歧，被迫延長。爭議的核心在於最新版協議草案中，刪除了所有關於化石燃料——即煤炭、石油與天然氣——的相關提法。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, the initial draft of the deal included strong language calling for a faster move away from fossil fuels. However, a second, shorter version released on Thursday surprised many by removing these references entirely and weakening goals related to electricity. This change has caused significant anger among various nations and civil society groups, who argue that the summit is failing to address the core causes of the climate crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，協議的初稿曾包含強硬措辭，呼籲加速淘汰化石燃料。然而，週四發布的第二版精簡草案卻讓許多人感到震驚，該版本不僅完全刪除了上述內容，還弱化了與電力相關的目標。此舉引發多國與公民社會團體的強烈憤怒，他們認為此次峰會未能解決氣候危機的根本原因。

paragraphs.en: Brazil’s national secretary for climate change, Aloisio Lopes Pereira de Melo, told reporters that at this stage, no one is happy with the current progress. The atmosphere at the summit has become increasingly tense. On Friday, a group of African ministers from countries including Ghana, Zambia, Senegal, Kenya, and Sierra Leone held a dramatic press conference. They stated that African people are being asked to pay for a climate crisis they did not cause. One minister emphasized their frustration, stating, “We didn’t come here to beg.”
paragraphs.zh: 巴西國家氣候變遷秘書阿洛伊西奧·洛佩斯·佩雷拉·德梅洛（Aloisio Lopes Pereira de Melo）向記者表示，現階段沒有人對目前的進展感到滿意。峰會現場氣氛日益緊張。週五，來自迦納、尚比亞、塞內加爾、肯亞與獅子山等國的非洲部長們召開了一場引人注目的記者會。他們指出，非洲人民被迫為自己並未造成的氣候危機買單。一位部長強調了他們的挫折感，表示：「我們來到這裡不是為了乞討。」

paragraphs.en: Several observers have pointed to Saudi Arabia as a country playing an obstructive role in the negotiations. The Guardian reported that Saudi Arabia is pushing for the final agreement to strongly reference carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS). CCUS is a technology designed to trap carbon dioxide emissions before they reach the atmosphere, which supporters say helps the planet meet the 1.5C temperature goal agreed upon in Paris. However, critics like Neil Grant, a senior expert at the advisory group Climate Analytics, described CCUS as a “Trojan horse” for fossil fuel interests, suggesting it is being used to keep the industry alive rather than replacing it with clean energy.
paragraphs.zh: 多位觀察家指出，沙烏地阿拉伯在談判中扮演了阻撓者的角色。《衛報》報導稱，沙烏地阿拉伯正極力推動在最終協議中強力納入「碳捕捉、利用與封存」（CCUS）技術。這是一項旨在於二氧化碳排放至大氣前將其捕獲的技術，支持者認為這有助於地球達成巴黎協定中設定的攝氏一點五度溫控目標。然而，氣候分析組織（Climate Analytics）的資深專家尼爾·格蘭特（Neil Grant）等批評者將 CCUS 稱為化石燃料利益集團的「特洛伊木馬」，認為該技術被用來延續產業壽命，而非以潔淨能源取而代之。

paragraphs.en: In response to the removal of fossil fuel language, a group of eight countries—including Panama, Belgium, Côte d’Ivoire, Finland, Greece, the Solomon Islands, and Sweden—have demanded that the text be restored. Juan Carlos Navarro, the climate minister for Panama, stated that it is unacceptable to have a final document that does not even mention fossil fuels. Panama has even sent an open letter to the president of the negotiations, Australian climate change minister Chris Bowen, outlining demands that the country considers non-negotiable.
paragraphs.zh: 針對化石燃料相關措辭被刪除一事，包括巴拿馬、比利時、象牙海岸、芬蘭、希臘、索羅門群島與瑞典在內的八個國家，已要求將相關內容恢復。巴拿馬氣候部長胡安·卡洛斯·納瓦羅（Juan Carlos Navarro）表示，一份連化石燃料都不敢提及的最終文件是無法接受的。巴拿馬甚至向談判主席、澳洲氣候變遷部長克里斯·鮑文（Chris Bowen）發出公開信，列出該國認為不可妥協的訴求。

paragraphs.en: Despite the clear divisions, Chris Bowen remains focused on finding a path forward. On Friday afternoon, he acknowledged that while people have strong views, the spirit of cooperation remains. “No one has said to me, let’s give up and go home,” Bowen told reporters. He noted that in any complex international negotiation, having firm positions—or “red lines”—is a normal part of the process.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管分歧明顯，克里斯·鮑文仍專注於尋找前進的方向。週五下午，他承認儘管各方立場強硬，但合作精神依然存在。鮑文告訴記者：「沒有人對我說要放棄並回家。」他指出，在任何複雜的國際談判中，擁有堅定的立場——即所謂的「紅線」——是過程中的正常現象。

paragraphs.en: Civil society groups, who have an official role in these talks, have been particularly vocal about their disappointment. They expressed frustration that a “just transition mechanism”—a plan intended to ensure that the shift to a low-carbon economy is fair for workers and poor communities—has not been moved forward. These groups have labeled the current event as the “worst Cop ever,” arguing that none of their main priorities have been included in the discussions.
paragraphs.zh: 在這些會談中扮演官方角色的公民社會團體，對此感到格外失望。他們對於旨在確保轉型至低碳經濟過程對勞工與貧困社區公平的「公正轉型機制」未能取得進展感到挫折。這些團體將此次大會稱為「史上最糟的氣候峰會」，並主張他們的主要訴求皆未被納入討論。

paragraphs.en: As the summit moves into the weekend, the pressure is mounting. Negotiators are expected to pore over a new draft of the agreement by Saturday morning. The challenge remains to find a middle ground that satisfies both the countries demanding urgent action on fossil fuels and those who are resisting such changes. Whether the summit can produce a meaningful result that helps the world avoid the worst effects of climate change remains to be seen. For now, the world is watching as the final hours of the summit unfold in Turkey, with the hope that a compromise can be reached to protect the future of the planet.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著峰會進入週末，壓力與日俱增。談判代表預計將在週六上午仔細審閱新版協議草案。挑戰在於如何找到一個折衷方案，既能滿足要求對化石燃料採取緊急行動的國家，又能安撫那些抵制變革的國家。此次峰會能否產生有意義的成果，協助全球避免氣候變遷帶來的最嚴重影響，仍有待觀察。目前，全世界都在關注土耳其峰會最後時刻的發展，期盼各方能達成妥協，以守護地球的未來。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A period of time beyond the scheduled or expected end of an event.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （活動或會議的）延長賽、超時階段。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於體育賽事或工作加班，這裡指會議超過原定時間。文中：The COP31 United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has entered a period of overtime as nearly 200 countries struggle to reach a final agreement.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To read or study something very carefully and in detail.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由 pore（鑽研）與 over 組成，非字面意思。文中：Negotiators are expected to pore over a new draft of the agreement by Saturday morning.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To increase in intensity or amount.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（山）或動詞（騎上/安裝），這裡指壓力逐漸升高。文中：As the summit moves into the weekend, the pressure is mounting.

quiz.question: What specific action did the group of eight countries, including Panama and Sweden, take in response to the latest draft of the agreement?

options.A: They held a press conference to demand the resignation of Chris Bowen.
options.B: They formally requested that the references to fossil fuels be put back into the text.
options.C: They threatened to leave the summit unless Saudi Arabia was removed from negotiations.
options.D: They proposed a new 'just transition mechanism' to support poor communities.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，這八個國家明確要求將關於化石燃料的內容恢復到協議草案中。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章中並未提到要求 Chris Bowen 辭職；選項 C 錯誤，雖然文章提到沙烏地阿拉伯的角色有爭議，但這並非這八國的具體訴求；選項 D 錯誤，儘管公民團體對「公平轉型機制」感到失望，但這並非這八國在第五段中提出的核心要求。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why are some nations and civil society groups particularly frustrated with the current state of the summit?

options.A: Because the summit was moved to Antalya, Turkey, which is inconvenient for many delegates.
options.B: Because they believe the current negotiations are ignoring the primary causes of the climate crisis.
options.C: Because they feel that carbon capture technology is being forced upon them by the United Nations.
options.D: Because the summit has officially ended without any agreement being signed by the participants.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，許多國家與公民團體認為刪除化石燃料相關內容是「未能解決氣候危機的核心原因」。選項 A 在文中未提及作為挫折來源；選項 C 錯誤，雖然對 CCUS 有爭議，但那是針對沙烏地阿拉伯的提議，而非導致所有人憤怒的唯一原因；選項 D 錯誤，文章提到會議進入「加班」階段，尚未正式結束或徹底失敗。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does Neil Grant imply by calling CCUS a "Trojan horse"?

options.A: It is a gift that will help developing nations transition to clean energy.
options.B: It is a dangerous technology that will cause immediate environmental damage.
options.C: It is a deceptive tool used to protect the fossil fuel industry under the guise of climate action.
options.D: It is an outdated method that has been proven ineffective in previous climate summits.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。「Trojan horse」（特洛伊木馬）在文中比喻一種表面上看起來有益（幫助達成 1.5C 目標），但實際上隱藏著破壞性意圖（維持化石燃料產業）的手段。選項 A 與文意完全相反；選項 B 錯誤，文中並未強調該技術會造成「立即性」的環境破壞，而是強調其對產業轉型的阻礙；選項 D 錯誤，文中並未提及該技術是否「過時」，重點在於其被利用的目的。

quiz.question: Which of the following best summarizes the central conflict of the COP31 summit described in the article?

options.A: The logistical difficulties of hosting a climate summit in Turkey during the weekend.
options.B: The personal disagreement between the Australian climate minister and African ministers.
options.C: The struggle to balance the demands for urgent action against fossil fuels with the resistance from certain nations and industry interests.
options.D: The failure of the United Nations to provide enough funding for the 'just transition mechanism' for workers.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於描述 COP31 面臨的僵局，主要源於各國對於是否應在協議中明確提及並淘汰「化石燃料」存在嚴重分歧，以及部分國家（如沙烏地阿拉伯）與要求採取緊急行動的國家之間的拉鋸。選項 A 為瑣事；選項 B 過度簡化了問題，忽略了結構性的利益衝突；選項 D 僅是眾多不滿中的一小部分，無法涵蓋全文關於化石燃料爭議的重點。
